title: Kingdom of Sweden
capsule: The Kingdom of Sweden coalesced as a unified Christian polity in the late tenth and eleventh centuries under kings such as Olof Skötkonung (r. c. 995–1022), who is credited with the first Swedish coinage. Sweden rose to major-power status during the seventeenth century, assembling a Baltic empire (Stormaktstiden) under Gustavus Adolphus (r. 1611–1632) that encompassed Finland, Estonia, Latvia, and Pomerania, before losing most of these territories to Russia after the Great Northern War ended at Nystad in 1721. The nineteenth century saw Sweden cede Finland to Russia (1809) and enter a peaceful union with Norway (1814–1905), thereafter consolidating as a constitutional monarchy. The kingdom remains a sovereign state to the present.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Swedish territorial extent from the medieval period onward is well documented by royal charters, tax rolls, and diplomatic treaties; early medieval boundaries in northern Scandinavia are approximate owing to sparse written sources and overlapping Sami territories.
